messages:
tara-support: FYI customer (FinScale) on private deployment sees API failures when calling models and our logs show repeated KMS decrypt 403s. They say audit events are missing too. tagging @security-oncall @sanjay @carla :rotating_light:
sanjay: Can you paste a repro? any recent config changes on their firewall/NAT?
tara-support: Repro from their app box attached below. They hit our endpoint and downstream KMS fails. Short logs:
```
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 POST /v1/generate 500 
error=KMS_DECRYPT_ERROR status=403 msg=Access denied to key projects/fin-kms/locations/global/keyRings/r1/cryptoKeys/serving-key
```
Steps they ran:
1) curl https://private-redwood.example.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer X" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
=> 500
2) from same host: curl -v https://kms.us-west1.provider.example/v1/projects/fin-kms:decrypt
=> ECONNREFUSED / TLS handshake failed
3) tcpdump shows outbound SYNs to kms.us-west1.provider.example but no SYN-ACK

tara-support: Customer says they have a locked-down egress policy (deny by default). Their firewall rules only allow outbound to corporate proxies and a few IP ranges. They did not whitelist our KMS endpoints or audit-collector endpoints.
carla: If egress is deny-by-default we'll definitely see missing audit events (we ship to audit collector over TLS). Two things to fix: allow KMS endpoints and allow audit ingestion endpoints + DNS/NTP. Also confirm their retention window; if logs were dropped and retention is 7 days we may not be able to reingest older events.
security-oncall: Agreed. Quick checks to run on their host: 
- curl -v https://kms.us-west1.provider.example:443
- openssl s_client -connect kms.us-west1.provider.example:443 -servername kms.us-west1.provider.example
- sudo iptables -L OUTPUT -v -n OR sudo nft list ruleset
If SYNs are leaving but no response, likely provider endpoint blocked by their perimeter. If SYN not even sent, local firewall blocking.
devops-jin: I asked for their NAT GW flow logs — they show REJECT for dst=52.12.34.56:443 from 10.3.12.45 multiple times between 09:11-09:14. That IP resolves to kms.us-west1.provider.example. So egress is being actively blocked.
security-oncall: For remediation we should give minimal allowlist rules. Example iptables snippet for them to add on the host or perimeter firewall: 
```bash
# allow redwood KMS endpoints
iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -p tcp -d 52.12.34.56 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT # DNS
iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -p udp --dport 123 -j ACCEPT # NTP
# allow audit collector (example)
iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -p tcp -d 198.51.100.45 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```
security-oncall: If they use a managed perimeter, they should add service-name-level egress rules to provider KMS hostnames and our audit collector FQDNs rather than IPs. Also call out HSM: if they integrated with an HSM proxy in their network, ensure that proxy can reach our key management replication endpoints on 443 and that TLS SNI is preserved.
carla: Billing note — missing audit events caused a parity check to flag a billing delta for model usage (we rely on audit ingestion for some metering). We should open a ticket to our billing ops to hold any invoice adjustments until logs are reingested or until we confirm usage with alternate traces.
tara-support: Filed internal ticket 6427 to billing ops and asked customer for a temporary waiver while we investigate. I also asked customer to capture a packet capture during attempted decrypt and share.
devops-jin: Quick workaround while they change perimeter: point their hosts to our egress proxy via an allowed corporate proxy that does allow outbound to those endpoints (we have a documented proxy tls passthrough config). Or add a NAT rule to allow outbound to the KMS IPs from their serving subnet. I can provide the proxy host + IP ranges if security approves.
security-oncall: Approve sharing proxy IPs for troubleshooting. Also recommend they run these validation commands after changes: 
```bash
# confirm TLS handshake to KMS
openssl s_client -connect kms.us-west1.provider.example:443 -servername kms.us-west1.provider.example 
# quickly test decrypt API (no key material)
curl -sS -X POST https://kms.us-west1.provider.example/v1/projects/fin-kms:decrypt -d '{}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
security-oncall: If they still get 403 afterwards, send KMS audit log lines (request_id) — 403 could be real IAM problem. But current evidence points to network egress blocking.
opsbot: deploy-bot: automated runbook check: runbook "private-vpc-egress-check" matched this thread; recommended playbook steps posted to ticket 6427.
sanjay: I'll set up a 30m call with the customer's network/security team at 15:00 PST to walk them through the allowlist changes and run the openssl checks live. I'll invite devops-jin and security-oncall.
tara-support: Thanks — will share the packet capture and their firewall policy before the call. We'll also ask them to temporarily increase log retention to 30 days in case reingest is needed.
carla: After remediation, we'll verify audit ingestion using our debug endpoint and then coordinate with billing ops to reconcile meter gaps.
sanjay: updating thread after call.
